title: Ripple Becomes a Bank: Will XRP Benefit?
description:
Will XRP benefit from Ripple becoming a regulated bank, or does RLUSD stablecoin make XRP irrelevant?
As a former investment banker, I analyze XRP through traditional finance frameworks. In this video:

Why XRP surged 500% in 2024 then crashed 63%
How Ripple's bank charter changes everything (but maybe not for XRP holders)
Three price scenarios: $0.80 to $5.00 over the next 12-18 months

By the end, you'll understand whether XRP is a genuine infrastructure play or just a coin that may lose relevance as Ripple the company succeeds.

0:00 Introduction
0:44 XRP Price Performance 2024-2026
2:23 XRP vs Bitcoin: Same Mission, Different Philosophy
3:33 Ripple's Transformation: Crypto Company → FinTech Bank
7:35 XRP Bear Case: 3 Major Risks
9:04 XRP Bull Case: 3 Bullish Catalysts
10:16 XRP Price Scenarios: $0.80 to $5.00 (2026-2027)
11:42 My Verdict: Ripple Wins, XRP Uncertain

asr.full_text: Hey everyone and welcome back to Crypto Partner Club. I am Mauro Terrinoli, former investment banker. Today we are analyzing XRP, one of the most controversial cryptocurrencies. In this video you are going to get three things. First, why XRP sur from Ripple becoming a regulated bank? And third, three specific price scenarios for XRP for the next 12 to 18 months. By the end, you'll understand whether XRP is a genuine infrastructure play or just a coin that may lose relevance. So let's dive in! XRP is currently trading between $1.30 and $1.40. In July 2025 XRP reached $3.65, its all-time high. Since then, XRP crashed 63%. So far this seems to be a story very similar to other coins we have seen, including Solana and Ethereum. But here's more! In December 2024, XRP was trading at 50 cents. similar to other coins we have seen including solana and ethereum but here there is more in december 2024 xrp was trading at 50 cents one month later it hit 2.60 a quintuple jump in just 30 days imagine get that trade for your portfolio five times your return in one month classic crypto now let me tell you the full story in december 2020 the SEC sued Ripple, the company behind XRP, alleging 1.3 billion in unregistered security sales, following the lawsuit XRP crushed to 20 cents major exchanges delisted it and for about 3-4 years XRP was essentially uninvestable in the u.s then news about the came out, that caused this extreme jump. And finally in August 2025 , the settlement with the SEC was formally announced. Ripple paid 125 million dollars, far less than the 2 billion dollars the SEC had sought in the lawsuit. The result is that XRP is now classified as a commodity, not as a security. And with this settlement, the regulatory overhang that kept institutional capital away from XRP for basically four years is gone. In the last few months, spot XRP ETFs have been launched and are starting to attract institutional and retail investors. So far, net ETF inflows have been in the region of 1.2 billion dollars. Let's now talk about the original vision behind XRP, and how that compares to Bitcoin to which it is often benchmarked. XRP and Bitcoin were designed to replace legacy payment rails but they have a radically different philosophy. Bitcoin's approach is pure decentralization there is no CEO, no company, no roadmap, its rigid and immutable by design bitcoin will do what bitcoin doubts no one controls it no one pivots it this is the story everyone knows xrp's approach is different ripple is a proper company it has leadership can do strategic pivots they can work with banks that can get regulated and adopt a strategy based on market conditions the difference is both XRP strengths and risk the strength is that Ripple can adapt when the SEC sued, they pivoted a strategy when stable coins emerged they launch their own stable coin Ripple USD RLUSD when bank regulation opened up they applied for a license that was the strength but the risk is that XRP holders are at the mercy of Ripple's management. If Ripple's leadership decides XRP is no longer central to their vision, the XRP holders cannot do anything about it. Now, let me tell you the story of Ripple's evolution, because it is critical to understanding whether XRP still matters. Ripple was founded in 2012 with the vision of creating Bitcoin without Mining. At the core there was the XRP Ledger, a blockchain that can sell transactions in 3-5 seconds with a fees is of $0.02. So two cents of a cent of a dollar. Essentially FREE and super FAST, faster and cheaper than Bitcoin. Then the founders created 100 billion XRP coins coins and allocated 80 billion coins to Ripple the company, and 20 billion coins went directly to the founders. The business model was based to convince banks and companies to use Ripple's payment platform called RippleNet and use XRP as an optional liquidity enabler. Then the SEC lawsuit hit in December 2020, and for three years Ripple was basically in a regulatory standoff. During that time the founders started exploring alternatives, and in December 2024 Ripple launched RLUSD, a stablecoin pegged to the US dollar. Then, in December 2025 Ripple received conditional approval from the OCC to establish a national trust-bank in the US. This means Ripple is becoming a federally-regulated financial institution. The bank licence allows Ripple to offer custody of digital assets under federal supervision, to manage reserves for RLUST and to access the Fed Wire payment system. This means that Ripple will become part of the banking payment system in The US. The mainly consequence of this is that Ripple is no longer just a Crypto company. It's becoming a Fed Tech bank, with Blockchain infrastructure. This is a massive event for Tech and Blockchain because it demonstrate the bridge between CR3D-FI and DEFI. For example a JPMorgan corporate client pays a supplier in the Philippines. Today, it uses SWIFT, which takes three to four days to settle and $50 in fees. With the Ripple Bridge, this client will make a Domestic Fedwire Transfer to Ripple National Trust Bank, which, through its blockchain, will credit the payment to the bank in the Philippines, all of which in 3 to 5 seconds and 1 cent of a dollar. Boom! Welcome to the new world of Global Payments! pins all of which in three to five seconds and one cent of the dollar boom welcome to the new world of global payments clearly instantaneous 24 7. this is the new infrastructure this is what blockchain can do tell your friends who think criptos is a scum but here's the key question in this new model where does xrp fit when ripple launched its stablecoin in December 2024, XRP's use case was challenged. XRP is not mandatory when banks use RippleNet. RippleUSD is a viable alternative. Today, RippleUSD has a market cap of $1.4 billion, and it has grown fast since launch. Large institutions including BlackRock, Deutsche Bank, Mastercard use RippleNet for settlements. Why would a bank choose XRP which swings 5-10% daily when they can use RLUSD which is back to the dollar as no volatility risk, as full regulatory clarity and widely considered and more understood and safer than a cryptocoin. So XRP has not disappeared but's existence has been weakened and so its use case. From a traditional finance perspective I always think where does the cash flow and try to position my investment as close as possible to the source of cash. Ripple the company will capture payment processing fees custody revenues banking margins, RLUSD transaction fees xrp the coin captures minimal transaction fees and no stake in yield unlike ethereum in investment banking terms you invest in the equity because that's where the value accrues in crypto you can only buy the coin but you need to be convinced of what is driving the coin price this is the dilemma that every xrp investor faces before we continue if you finding this analysis helpful, hit subscribe, I post weekly videos analyzing crypto through traditional finance frameworks. No hype, no paid promotions … just fundamentals. Now let me give you the bear case on XRP, 3 structural problems. bearish risk 1. Ripple USD Cannibalisation As explained, RLUSD directly replaces XRP use case. Banks prefer stable coins with zero volatility rather than a volatile coin like XRP. If RLUSD adoption accelerates, XRP may become economically irrelevant. Bearish risk 2 XRP becoming optional in Ripple's business model. Ripple claims 300 plus financial institutions use RippleNet. That sounds impressive, but here's the reality. Only about 40% of those clients actually use XRP for on-demand liquidity and therefore 60% of clients use RippleNet without touching XRP. XRP can grow as a network while XRP transactions may fall because the it is optional the whole use case of eXRP is in my view severely undermined bearish RISK-3 supply overhang the founders and Ripple the company holds 50B eXRP coins which at current prices worth about 70B in traditional finance this is like stock with 20% public load and 80% insider control. Insiders support the price but they also have a value in mind when they want to monetize. This creates uncertainty, if founders decide to sell aggressively at 3, 5, 8 USD, the upside is capped. The supply overhang may cap the return for investors and create constant selling pressure. Now let's look at the bulls case and why this could still work bullish catalyst one xrp becomes popular for exotic currency pairs even if RLUSD is better placed to handle stable settlement XRP may be needed for liquidity bridges in exotic currency pairs for example the philippine pesos or other less mainstream currencies in those cases the ruipple stablecoin may not have enough liquidity, and therefore XRP could be a better option. Bullish catalyst number two the founders and Ripple the company have 50-billion XRP coins worth $70-billion at current market prices. The are economically aligned with XRP holders. They should not let XRP go to zero. They have a massive financial incentive to support the price. The question is at which level will they support it? Do they support it at $3? $5? $8? We don't know, but that holding creates a floor but also a ceiling. Bullish Catalyst III. Regulatory Clarity. XRP ETs have attracted so far $.2 billion dollars since launch in november 2025 this is a legitimate institutional demand for this coin further annual inflows could push xrp to a new all-time high this is the bull case let me now give you three price scenarios for xrp for the next 12 to 18 months scenario 1 downside case 80 cents to a dollar 20. in this scenario rl usd fully replaces xrp for payments banks choose stable coins over volatile bridge assets ripple net grows but xrp usage declines founders begin aggressive selling to monetize holdings macro environment worsens fed holds rates rates high, recession fears return. as a consequence, XRP drops to $0.80, to $1.2, back below pre rally levels. scenario 2, base case, $1.50 to $2.50, in this scenario , XRP coexists with RL USD, some liquidity corridors use XRP, most use RL USD. Ripple Bank charter approved approved moderate institutional etfs inflows continue founders support the price but also monetize periodically xrp trades in the range a dollar fifty to two dollars fifty scenario three upside case dollars to five dollars in this scenario institutional demand accelerates etf inflows reach 5 to 8 billion annually. Ripple secures FedMaster account. • XRP becomes required for certain liquidity corridors. • Founders actively support price, with minimal selling. • XRP reaches $ 3 to 5 potentially aiming towards new all-time highs. So, here is my verdict as a former investment banker Ripley will succeed in bridging defy and tread fight i have high confidence in that they have the bank charter they have the institutional network they have the regulatory clarity they have the vision and the execution capability Gripple the company will win but will XRP the coin benefit that's uncertain here's the dilemma if I could invest in in Ripple the equity, I would choose that over XRP any time. Why? Because cash flows accrue to the equity, not the coin, while Ripple will earn revenues from payment processing fees, custody services, banking margins Ripple's stablecoin interest rate margin, XRP only earns minimal transaction fees fees and not staking yields... So Ripple's growth story doesn't necessarily drive Exorpi's price. The upside case exists! If institutions mandate Exorpi for liquidity, and funders aggressively support the price, we may see new all-time highs. But this is a highly uncertain bet in my view. You are not just betting on Ripple's success, you are betting on whether XRP remains central to the vision of the founders.
